text:
jonathan: quick dump from this morning's kernel-decider run — found some odd behavior switching between triton and cutlass paths for mid-length sequences (96-256).

kai: curious — what do the perf numbers look like?

jonathan: ran a profiling sweep on A100 + 8k context models. summary: triton wins <64 and >512, cutlass/CUDA wins consistently 96-256 on batch sizes 1-8.

maria: is that with KV cache active?

jonathan: yes, KV cache enabled. interestingly, when the KV cache hit rate is high the triton path regresses ~6-8% on tail latency vs cutlass for 128 tokens. suspect memory access pattern + small-kv-evictions.

kai: can you paste the minimal repro command?

jonathan: sure:
```bash
# repro profile
python perf_run.py --model gptx-8k --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8 --seqlens 32,64,96,128,256,512 --kv on --profile
```

jonathan: sample CSV row: model,gpu,seqlen,batch,avg_p50,avg_p95
gptx-8k,A100,128,1,78.2,210.6
gptx-8k,A100,128,1 (cutlass),71.4,195.2

maria: hmm those are significant. Did autotune pick different kernels based on seqlen?

jonathan: yes — the decider selected triton.conv for seqlen <=64, triton.mha for >512, but for 96-256 it toggled between triton and cutlass every few runs — because our hysteresis window is too narrow.

infra-bot: [deploy-notice] autotune-config v1.12 pushed to staging at 1778806200

kai: toggling kernel choices per-run is bad for p95 stability. we should consider sticky assignments per-model+seqlen-range with a TTL.

sara: Agreed. Also we need to surface a metric: "switch_count" per model variant so we can detect flapping.

jonathan: added. I also captured a perf trace showing increased memcpy calls in the triton path when KV is hot — attaching snippet:
```
# from perf trace
memcpy_backward  1.2ms  (frequent)
evict_kv_buffer 0.9ms
triton_launch   3.5ms
cutlass_launch  2.8ms
```

maria: that points to kernel memory layout differences. cutlass seems to keep working set more compact for mid seqlens.

kai: short-term mitigation: add a rule to prefer cutlass for seqlen in [96,256] when kv_hit_rate > 0.7 and batch <=8. Long-term: expand autotuner to include kv_hit_rate and avg_ctx_len as features.

jonathan: implemented a rule prototype on staging. initial A/B shows p95 down 12% for the affected slices.

sara: important to make sure we don't regress throughput for larger batches. did you test batch=32?

jonathan: yes — batch=32 still prefers triton and we preserved throughput. the decision tree: if batch >= 16 -> triton; else follow kv-hit + seqlen rule.

maria: what's next action items?

jonathan: 1) roll the seqlen+kv rule to canary traffic for 24h (i'll queue)
2) add switch_count telemetry & alert if >3/hour per model
3) expand autotune feature vector to include kv_hit_rate and avg_ctx_len (tracking issue: #INF-482)
4) schedule a micro-arch session with kernel authors to examine memcpy hotspots

kai: ping me when canary starts. If canary looks good, we can bake rule into v1.13 autotune and widen hysteresis.

infra-bot: [canary-start] kernel-decider-rule roll to 5% at 1778807000

sara: thanks team. small ask — document the rule somewhere in the runtime README so oncall knows why routing changed.

jonathan: will do. adding a short blurb to the runtime docs and linking the perf CSVs.

kai: nice work. cc @maria for the kernel follow-up meeting.
